migration.description: Persist OIDC identities, server-side SCS session payloads and revocable user API credentials.

durable_state.description: The candidate creates user identities keyed by OIDC issuer and subject, opaque server-side session payloads, and hashed API credential records. Raw bearer credentials are returned only at creation and are never stored.
durable_state.storage_implementation: PostgreSQL tables managed by the embedded Goose migration history; SCS uses auth_sessions as its Store.

source_compatibility_range.from_program_version: Phase-one infrastructure candidate before migration 00003; no earlier business-auth state is supported.
source_compatibility_range.earlier_state: The absent tables are treated as unapplied migrations and the candidate is not ready until migration 00003 commits.

ordered_operations.description: Create auth_users, auth_sessions and auth_api_credentials with issuer/subject uniqueness, opaque session expiry and one-way credential hash storage.

rollout_signals: Goose records migration 00003 before Server readiness is exposed.
Credential lookup requires revoked_at IS NULL and session lookup requires expiry > CURRENT_TIMESTAMP.

validation: OIDC identities are idempotently upserted by issuer and subject.
Session payloads survive database close and reopen and expired sessions are not returned.
A newly created credential authenticates, a revoked credential is rejected immediately, and the raw token is absent from stored rows and logs.
